description.narrative:
This project supports the responsible growth of SORDO’s youth-led green social enterprise model in Puntland, Somalia and Somaliland. It strengthens existing income-generating activities in climate-smart agriculture, eco-services, and green value chains managed byyoung people aged 18–35. The project focuses on improving enterprise systems, market access, and financial sustainability while expanding employment opportunities for marginalized youth, particularly displaced youth and young women. Through enterprise coaching, market linkage development, and institutional capacity strengthening, the project increases enterprise revenues and reinvests surpluses into youth employment, skills development, and environmental impact—reducing reliance on donor funding and ensuring long-term sustainability. The project will sustainably increase income for youth-led enterprises, create stable green jobs, and strengthen youth economic leadership. Reinvested enterprise revenues will support continued employment, skills development, and climate-positive livelihoods for marginalized young people. Enterprise revenues will continue beyond the grant period, with profits reinvested into expansion, youth employment, and operational costs. Strengthened business systems, market contracts, and partnerships will ensure continuity without donor dependence.
Goal: Strengthen the financial sustainability and growth of SORDO’s Youth Empowerment and Social Enterprises (YESS) program which is a youth-led green social enterprise.
Objectives: Improve enterprise management and financial systems. Expand market access and value chains. Increase youth employment and income.
Key Activities: Business diagnostics, enterprise coaching, market linkage development, financial systems strengthening, youth leadership training, and peer learning.

participating-org.narrative: The Somali Relief and Development Organization (SORDO) is a youth-led, non-profit social enterprise dedicated to creating sustainable economic opportunities for young people in Somalia, with a strong focus on climate resilience, green livelihoods, and social inclusion. Guided by the principle “Creating Local Solutions to Local Challenges,” SORDO combines community-based development with income-generating social enterprise models that reinvest profits into youth employment and environmental impact. SORDOis governed and ledentirely by young people aged 18–35, with over 50% women representation in leadership and management. The organization operates youth-led green enterprises across Puntland and other regions, including climate-smart agriculture value chains, eco-services, renewable energy solutions, and youth eco-hubs. These enterprises generate income that supports youth employment, skills development, and reinvestment into community programmes. Over the past five years, SORDO has implemented more than 20 youth-focused projects with partners including NCA, IsDB, UNHCR, UNDP, FAO, Global Youth Mobilization, and the Italian Ministry of Environment and Climate Security. Through its social enterprise activities, SORDO has trained and employed over 1,400 young people—prioritising displaced youth, ruralyouth, and young women—while strengthening organisational sustainability beyond donor funding.
